title.narrative: Hubei Jingzhou Historic Town Conservation Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Hubei Jingzhou Historic Town Conservation Project for China is to conserve cultural heritage and improve water quality and tourism services in selected areas in Jingzhou Municipality. There are four components to the project, the first component being cultural heritage conservation and tourism services improvement. The second component is the water environment improvement. The third component is the water environment improvement. This component aims to facilitate access to the cultural heritage sites for residents and tourists alike by improving NMT and public transport options. It will also help improve movement of tourists by upgrading signage. Finally, the fourth component is the assistance to project management and capacity building. This component aims to strengthen the technical and institutional capacity of the Project Management Office (PMO) and the Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs): provision of support for project management, monitoring, and supervision and independent monitoring of environmental and social safeguards, including the provision of office equipment and supplies; carrying out of capacity building activities, including training, organization of workshops and study tours for relevant staff and key stakeholders; and Provision of technical assistance, including the realization of studies on conservation and restoration of historic sites and neighborhoods, as well as on traffic management for Jingzhou's historic town.
To conserve cultural heritage and improve water quality and tourism services in selected areas in Jingzhou Municipality.

title.narrative: Heritage display space upgraded or created

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved (100%). The result reflects the rehabilitation of 10.2 kilometers of the inner ring road at the foot of thehistoric city wall, as well as improvements to pedestrian paths, bike lanes, bus stations, drainage, and sewage network along the inner ring road. </p>
<p>Information source: review of Jingzhou Construction Management Center's report.</p>

title.narrative: City Wall restored under the project

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved (100%). The restoration of the 11.28-kilometer City Wall included the construction of a retaining wall, landscaping, and vegetation improvements, and the pavement of the wall-top footpath. </p>
<p>Information source: Visit to sites during the ICR Mission.</p>

<p>Target achieved (100%). The result reflects the upgrading of 12 pedestrian crossings at six junctions inside the JHT to enhance the safety of non-motorized transportation (walking and biking). The project financed the improvement of the transportation signage system (installed amber flashings, repainted pedestrian crossings, installed speed limit signs) and the improvement of the transportation management facilities.</p>
<p> Information source: review of Jingzhou Traffic Management Bureau’s report.</p>

<p>Target achieved (100%). Twenty-eight bus stops were satisfactorily upgraded in 2019, including their boards and kiosks. Thebus stops are located both inside the JHT and along the new bus route between the JHT and Xiongjiazhong Archeological Park.</p>
<p>Information source: review of data submitted by the Jingzhou Public Transport Company Limited.</p>

title.narrative: Dredging of the moat and lakes with safe storage /disposal of the dredged materials

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved (100%). The dredged materials were disposed of at Yutaicun Landfill. Based on assessments conducted by an independent consultant and the review of the landfill closure actions recorded by the local ecological environment bureau, the dredged material is safely stored in Yutaicun Landfill. </p>
<p>Information source: Borrower’s completion report, confirmed by World Bank reports.</p>

title.narrative: Participants in consultation activities during project implementation (number)

comment.narrative:
<p>Target exceeded (128%). Participants were tourists who participated in the tourist satisfaction survey as well as local residents and tourists who participated in the Environment Effect Assessment. </p>
<p>Information source: review of the report from Easen Group.</p>

title.narrative: Cultural heritage sites conserved/rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved (100%). The five cultural heritage sites conserved/rehabilitated are the City Wall, the Kaiyuan Taoism Temple, Jingzhou Museum’s Treasure Pavilion, the Xiongjiazhong Archeological Park, and selected historic buildings. 1. Jingzhou's Historic City Wall works included the conservation of the Earth City Wall and the West City Wall and the pavement of the wall-top footpath; 2. Kaiyuan Taoism Temple works included stone tablets preservation and exhibition and environment improvements; 3. Conservation activities in Jingzhou Museum included equipment upgrades and environment improvements for Jingzhou Museum; 4. Xiongjiazhong Archeological Park works included infrastructure and landscape improvement of the Park, construction of the Exhibition Center of Unearthed Cultural Relics (new building), and upgrade of the Exhibition of Horse-chariots Pits and Sacrifice Pits; 5. Conserved and regenerated 11 selected historic buildings along Dongti Street and Nanmen Street.</p>
<p>Information source: Visit to sites during the ICR Mission.</p>

<p>Target exceeded (110%). Beneficiaries were local residents (166,800 females and 173,200 males) in and tourists to Jingzhou (208,886 females and 201,114 males). They benefitted from a better urban environment (especially the clean moat around JingzhouHistoric City), the conserved heritage sites (including the City Wall, the Kaiyuan Taoist Temple, the Treasure Pavilion of the Jingzhou Museum, the Xiongjiazhong Archeological Park, as well as the selected historic buildings), better-managed transportation withinthe historic city, as well as bus services to sites outside the city. </p>
<p>Information source: Project management consultant reports the 7th National Census of 2020.</p>

title.narrative: Participants rated the training/study tours good or excellent

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved (100%). Training satisfaction surveys were conducted on June 12, 2017, August 30, 2017, July 4, 2018, November 9, 2018, December 20, 2019, and February 8, 2022. Eighty percent of the participants rated project-financed training satisfactory. </p>
<p>Information source: Project management consultant report. </p>

title.narrative: Wastewater interceptors constructed inside and outside of the moat

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved (100.2%). The project financed the construction of 8,317.2 meters of interceptors inside the JHT moat and 162.8 meters of interceptors outside of JHT moat. </p>
<p>Information source: Jingzhou District Government.</p>

title.narrative: Satisfaction of tourists on tourism services in Jingzhou Historic Town (JHT)

comment.narrative:
<p>Target exceeded (109%). 92.9% is the score for “Overall impression on this travel in Jingzhou,” which is the averagescore of 6 indicators, including Publicity and promotion of the Jingzhou Historic Town, Tourist site management and service, Tour safety, Completeness of tourist service facilities, Convenience of transport, Conservation and renovation of Jingzhou Historic Town and cultural relics, and Tourism value of the Jingzhou Historic Town. </p>
<p>Information source: Tourist satisfaction survey carried out by the independent consultant engaged by the Jingzhou Municipality, in October 2022.</p>

title.narrative: Moat water meets Class IV for BOD (< 6 mg/l) for at least 10 of the 12 monthly samples per year

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved (100%). Monthly monitoring (field investigation, sample collection, and analysis) was carried out by a third party, the Hubei Provincial Academy of Environmental Sciences, as well as the Jingzhou District Environmental Bureau. The two sources showed that the quality markedly improved to Class IV for BOD (< 6 mg/l) following the completion of the dredging and interceptor construction works.</p>
<p>Information source: Borrower's completion report, confirmed by World Bank reports.</p>
